description: Test vectors for a client port of certificate pinning and pairing-payload validation ([X1.1], docs/analisis/lo-que-viene-del-servidor-2026-09-13.md of the movieIndexAndroid repository). A phone trusts the certificate presented over TLS only if the pin it derives matches the one carried in the QR payload, using the same SPKI derivation as the server; tests/test_pairing_certificate_vectors.py recomputes every value here from the server's own functions, so a change that would change what a phone accepts fails this suite.

generator.spki_pin: SHA-256 of the certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo (the whole ASN.1 substructure, not just the key bytes), base64-encoded with padding: openssl x509 -pubkey -noout | openssl pkey -pubin -outform der | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | openssl enc -base64. 32 bytes -> 44 base64 characters, one trailing '='.
generator.qr_payload: The four fields a QR carries -- origin, ticket, account, and certificate_pin when the instance has one -- JSON-encoded with no whitespace (separators ',' and ':'), UTF-8. fits_in_qr is true when the encoded byte length is at most max_payload_bytes.

certificates.label: ec_p256_short_form_der_length
certificates.description: P-256, CN=casa.local, OpenSSL 3.5.7, generated 2026-09-09. Real, throwaway, self-signed; no private key was ever committed. Its SubjectPublicKeyInfo is short enough for a single-byte DER length -- the common case.

certificates.label: rsa_2048_long_form_der_length
certificates.description: RSA-2048, CN=192.168.1.50 with an IP SAN, OpenSSL 3.5.7, generated 2026-09-09. Real, throwaway, self-signed; no private key was ever committed. Its SubjectPublicKeyInfo needs a long-form DER length, which the EC one above does not exercise -- the shape a hand-written parser is most likely to get wrong.
